content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: front-loaded general overtime, a short break delay and chat deflection on both queues lift service level to 80.4% for 11:45-15:30, just above the 80% target, for ₹18,441.","why":"A 10:50 regional TV ad for the zero-balance savings account pushed general calls to 122-124 per interval against about 79 forecast. New-offer calls are at 3.7x normal, service level fell to 4.8%, and 48 calls have been abandoned. Staffing and absences are on plan, so this is a demand problem. R2 adds overtime: 28 general agents 12:15-14:15 and 16 agents 14:15-15:45. It delays general breaks (11:45-12:15) by 45 minutes. It deflects 20% of new-offer and balance enquiries on general, and 20% of payment-status and refund enquiries on payments, to chat. It also adds IVR callback on general and cancels the 15:30 coaching. It does not move cross-skilled agents off payments. Predicted results for the window: overall 80.4%, payments 86.7%, general 75.0%, abandons 3.9%. Rest of day is expected at 88.1%. It is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches 80%. No escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["R1 predicts 82.9% (general 78.8%, abandons 3.6%) for ₹180 more (₹18,621). It gives more margin above target if you prefer a buffer.","P3 and P4 (₹16,641) save about ₹1,800 but reach only 73.0% and 71.9%. Both move 4 agents off payments, holding payments at about 76%.","The low-cost plans P1 and P2 (₹825 and ₹1,701) do no better than no action (38.7%). General stays around 13-16% and payments drop to about 61%.","R2 clears the target by only 0.4 points, and general itself is predicted at 75.0%, below 80%."],"watch":"R2 depends on overtime uptake, especially the 28 agents for 12:15-14:15, and on the break delay holding. If uptake falls short, or new-offer calls keep rising after 12:00, general will drop below target quickly. In that case, switch to R1 or add more overtime."}
